sentences.text:
This appeal has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 20/02/2019 passed in MACC No.61/2017 by 4th Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chhatarpur seeking reduction of compensation.
2.

Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submits that in para-12 of impugned award, Tribunal has determined permanent disability as 10%, still, Tribunal has awarded Rs.3,00,000/-, after referring and relying upon Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd. and Another, (2014) 14 SCC 396 .

entities.text: Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd. and Another, (2014) 14 SCC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As claimant suffered 10% permanent disability, therefore, in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Mallikarjun (supra),
claimant was entitled to receive Rs.1,00,000/- excluding compensation under other heads.

Therefore, compensation awarded by the Tribunal be reduced by Rs.2,00,000/-
3.

Learned counsel on behalf of respondent No.1/claimant submits NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:16878 2 MA-2864-2019 that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
It is also urged that in para- 11 of impugned awarded, Dr.Mahesh Pahadia has deposed that complainant suffered 40% permanent disability.
But Tribunal wrongly determined 10% permanent disability.
Hence, compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and no reduction is required in the same.
Hence, appeal filed by the appellant/Insurance company be dismissed.

sentences.text: 1 4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.

5. So far as principle of law laid down in Mallikarjun (supra) is concerned, perusal of the same reveals that aforesaid pronouncement relates to compensation whenever any child suffered any disability in Motor Vehicle Accident.
Present case relates to claimant, who was student of B.A. (IV semester) and at the time of accident, she was aged approximately 18 years.
Therefore, principle of law laid down i n Mallikarjun (supra) would not apply to the facts of the case.

Hence, Tribunal has erred in determining compensation after relying upon Mallikarju (supra).
6.
Perusal of facts reveals that in the instant case, Tribunal has not awarded any amount for loss of future earnings.
On the date of accident, claimant was aged 18 years.

On the date of accident,
minimum wages of an unskilled labour were Rs.4,945/- per month.
7. In view of age of applicant, 40% is to be added as future prospect and multiplier of 18 is to be applied.

In the instant case, as per findings recorded by the Tribunal in para-12 of impugned award,
Tribunal has determined 10% permanent disability.

8. Hence, in view of aforesaid, claimant is entitled to receive NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:16878 3 MA-2864-2019 Rs.1,49,688/- as loss for future earnings.

Therefore,
compensation awarded by Tribunal is reduced by Rs.1,50,312/- (Rs.3,00,000/- - Rs.1,49,688/-).
9.
Hence, compensation awarded by the Tribunal is reduced by Rs.1,50,312/-.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
10. Appeal filed by the appellant/insurance company is accordingly allowed and disposed off.
11. Record of Tribunal be sent back.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE sm L. N. T. General Insurance Company Ltd. vs Kiran Kushwaha on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24053873/
